The flat-welded and stressed (u-bend) welded coupons post cleaning procedure were cross-sectioned and analyzed using optical microscopy to assess intergranular attack. Figure 14 highlights polished microstructures of the cross-sectioned flat-welded coupons. The condition of the as-polished cross sections displayed little evidence of subsurface cracking, damage, or defects. The surface damage itself is relatively minor, with small signs of pitting in the stainless-steel coupons ranging from 10 to 15 microns in depth. The surface of the SA 516-70 plate steel showed greater surface damage with pits as large as 20 to 30 microns in depth, but no localized attack on any of the coupons was detected. Figure 15 shows cross sections of the flat-welded coupons for the three stainless alloys that were etched to reveal more details in the microstructure. In the base metal, only the highest energy grain boundaries such as twin and slip plains were made visible from the etching, whereas the weld and HAZ were clearly visible. Across alloys, no major signs of damage in or around the weld were observed. Small differences in the microstructural appearance were due to variations in etching and alloy composition. Figure 14: Surfaces of polished flat-welded coupon cross-sections (Mag: 200x) Figure 16a shows the U-bend coupon cross-section of a SS 316L coupon. Unlike other coupons examined to this point, this U-bend was cross-sectioned down the length of the weld giving a look at how the weld surface performed in the test environment. The surface of the weld fared approximately the same as the exposed base metal, but the micrographs revealed features in the HAZ that were the focus of higher magnification analysis in Figure 16b. Of note, the etching revealed small signs of sensitization of the grains near the weld and in the HAZ. Figure 16b shows the formation of chromium carbides and chromium depletion zones in the microstructure. These features appear attributable to the welding process itself rather than corrosion exposure. No significant sensitization or localized attack resulting from molten sulfur exposure was observed along the weld or HAZ. Page 32 of 87 DE-EE0009329 Element 16 Technologies, Inc.
